subject: Climate & Environment
title: Megacities and Their Challenges
description: A 60-second lesson on Megacities and Their Challenges.

hook.text: A megacity has over 10 million people. There are now 33 of them — and the number is growing.

buildup.text: Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai, and São Paulo each house more people than many entire countries.

discovery.text: Megacities face extreme pressure on water, sanitation, housing, and transport systems.

twist.text: Most future megacity growth will happen in Africa and South Asia — regions with the fewest resources.

climax.text: Planning now for infrastructure that doesn't yet exist is the biggest opportunity.

punchline.text: Tomorrow's megacities haven't been built yet. That's the chance.

quiz.question: How many megacities exist in the world today?

details.summary: Megacities with over 10 million residents face acute challenges including traffic congestion, air pollution, water stress, and waste overload. There are now over 30 megacities worldwide, and their infrastructure often struggles to keep pace with rapid population growth and climate pressures.
details.whyItMatters: Megacities are laboratories for sustainability solutions at scale. Their successes and failures in managing resources and emissions have outsized global impact.
takeaways: Over 30 cities now have populations exceeding 10 million
Rapid growth outpaces infrastructure in many megacities
Air quality and water access are critical challenges

faq.question: What is the world's largest megacity?
faq.answer: Tokyo is the largest metropolitan area with about 37 million residents, followed by Delhi, Shanghai, and Sao Paulo. By 2030, Delhi is projected to overtake Tokyo as the world's most populous urban agglomeration.

faq.question: How do megacities manage waste?
faq.answer: Many megacities struggle with waste management, relying on landfills and open dumps. Advanced cities like Tokyo achieve recycling rates above 40 percent through strict sorting rules, while poorer megacities often depend on informal waste pickers for material recovery.
